parent.title: Extending Claude Code: MCP, Skills, Plugins — a session-3 blueprint

siblings.title: MCP deep-dive
siblings.summary: Talk-prep brief for a 1–2 hour deep-dive on the Model Context Protocol — architecture, 2026 spec, ecosystem, security trifecta, and live-demo recipes.

siblings.title: Claude Code Skills
siblings.summary: A Skill is a Markdown file + optional bundled scripts that Claude loads on demand. Cheaper than CLAUDE.md, more discoverable than a slash command, lighter than a subagent — and now an open cross-vendor standard.

siblings.title: Plugins & the Marketplace
siblings.summary: What plugins actually are, how the official + community marketplaces work, the few that earn their keep, and the trust footgun to flag in any 1–2 hour deep-dive.

siblings.title: Subagents, hooks, and the rest of the harness
siblings.summary: One-page mental model for teaching Claude Code's harness: subagents (isolation), hooks (determinism), and the config substrate (skills, permissions, settings).

siblings.title: Session delivery plan
siblings.summary: A 90-minute run-of-show with 8-12 min active blocks, mid-session recap, and series-continuity callbacks tuned for the third session in a deep-dive series.

sources.title: airfocus — Weighted decision matrix for prioritization
sources.claim: Weighted decision matrix: score each option per criterion, multiply by weight, sum — highest total wins.

sources.title: The Forum Launcher — Running a topic-expert deep-dive
sources.claim: Topics land when matched to the group's current pain point, not the presenter's interest; internal speakers with lived experience beat external experts presenting researched material.

sources.title: Tempo — Weighted scoring model
sources.claim: Weights must sum to 100%; cap criteria at ~4; never change criteria mid-evaluation; lock weights before viewing candidates to avoid gaming.

sources.title: Certlibrary — Choosing a technical presentation topic
sources.claim: Authentic, lived material beats researched material; pick what the presenter has actually shipped.

sources.title: Intercom — RICE: simple prioritization for product managers
sources.claim: RICE = (Reach × Impact × Confidence) / Effort, built by Intercom to compare product-feature ideas where reach is customers/quarter and effort is person-months.

sources.title: Whatfix — RICE scoring model
sources.claim: RICE's reach and effort axes degenerate for fixed-audience, fixed-duration sessions — the framework keeps scoring but stops discriminating.

sources.title: FourWeekMBA — Frameworks for decision-making
sources.claim: Weighted scoring is the more flexible choice when criteria are domain-specific rather than product-feature shaped.
